essential_tweet_embeddings.annotation: Theoretical artifact: Morphic resonance as 'model organism of woo theories'—simple, mechanismless, explains everything (or nothing)
essential_tweet_embeddings.tweet_text: i find i have such a soft spot for sheldrake's morphic resonance theory not just because it has a great name but also because it's simple and makes no claims (afaik) as to any underlying mechanism which would enable it. it's a model organism of woo theories of everything.under my interpretation, it says: there is a subtle bias to all physical systems in the universe. spatiotemporal patterns which have happened before "want" to occur again.this can apparently be used to explain a wide variety of woo phenomena from telepathy to how fake cattle grids work (https://t.co/XmRj2Kc3du). the idea is that this subtle bias is strong enough that brain states in one organism would develop similarity to brain states from other (similar) organisms be they contemporaneous or from the past, and so their internal states and patterns of behaviour would develop similarities too. like magical nonlocal canalisation. (you would expect to see these effects accumulate faster in systems with dynamics close to criticality)to what extent is this theory equivalent to saying, "a wizard did it"? if it can explain anything doesn't it also explain nothing? what's the negative space – are there any woo phenomena which you *couldn't* explain using morphic resonance?

essential_tweet_embeddings.annotation: Contemporary synthesis: Science as 'historically obedient,' always catching up to reality—ancient modalities worked before peer review existed
essential_tweet_embeddings.tweet_text:
if you only believe in science, you might be falling behind… because empirical science is always catching up to reality.

science, in its modern form, is reactive, not generative. It waits for a phenomenon to present itself repeatedly, then tries to explain it through observation and replication.

but reality - especially consciousness, nonlinear time, entanglement, energy fields - doesn’t give a damn about what science is ready to measure.

It just is.

So if your worldview is limited to “what has already been proven,” you're essentially living in a historical version of reality.

---

for decades, “rational thinkers” dismissed intuition as woo.

but now, Neuroscience shows the gut has 100 million neurons, and the heart emits a measurable electromagnetic field.

the body thinks, and intuition isnt something mythic, it’s precognitive pattern detection.

it's signal before words

and science still can’t explain what consciousness is, only that it appears to be “produced” by the brain.

meanwhile, ancient systems said consciousness is fundamental, and recent theories (like integrated information theory or quantum consciousness models) are slowly walking back toward that.

acupuncture, reiki, breathwork, EMDR, and field-based healing were ridiculed for years.

now science is crawling behind with vagal nerve studies, epigenetic reprogramming, and brainwave entrainment.

ancient modalities were working long before we had peer-reviewed journals.

Science is always late to the party it wasn’t invited to.

so if you wait for science to confirm something before believing it’s real, you’re not being logical

you’re being historically OBEDIENT.
